newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Power takes steps after blast.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Power takes steps after blast.

text.p: Scottish Power Plc said it would temporarily ban certain switches used to avoid downtime while changing power supplies as a result of early inquiries into a blast at a sub-station which killed two men.
A spokesman for the company said the ban would run for the duration of inquiries, which started on Wednesday.
"It looks on the surface as if they were killed in an explosion using oil switches, so that is the area to look at primarily," the spokesman said.
David Dryden, aged 30 and Innes McKinnon, 28, died after the explosion hit the unit near Glasgow, Scotland, at 1800 GMT on Tuesday.
Jason Reynolds, aged 29, was injured in the blast and remains "comfortable" in the burns unit of Glasgow's Royal Infirmary.
The spokesman said the ban on the oil switches would mean using slower methods, which could lead to some delays in restoring supplies but added that it was unlikely to be noticeable to consumers.
"Oil switches are a swift way of restoring supplies, other procedures could take longer," he said.
Scottish Power said it had advised other electricity companies in Britain of its proposed ban.
